A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Existing material can be matched across the layout changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original distance-prediction, sorting-network satisfiability and circuit-property experiments in Section 5, with additional experimental results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports no-PE controls in Table 3 and a SAT distance-prediction comparison in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The Multi-q Magnetic Laplacian construction and complex-domain stable PE processing in Section 4 are unchanged. The added SAT evaluation uses the existing encodings without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover synthetic directed and acyclic graphs, sorting networks, Open Circuit Benchmark and high-level synthesis. The new Appendix F evaluates already covered DAG distance and walk-profile tasks using another backbone.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds a no-PE comparator for each of four backbones: undirected GIN, bidirected GIN and their SAT variants. The previously evaluated PE comparators remain present.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds a reported DAG distance evaluation using SAT with a bidirectional GIN encoder and SPE processing. The original MLP-based distance experiment remains, and existing splits, metrics, budgets and hyperparameter tables are unchanged.

E4.justification: The added no-PE controls test the benefit of including positional encodings. Appendix F also examines whether a stronger graph-transformer backbone addresses older encodings' distance-prediction limitations. Existing q-selection, generalization and runtime analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 replaces overall-best dagger annotations with stars indicating that the best result exceeds the runner-up by one standard deviation. This adds a comparison based on reported variability. Existing seed counts and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged; no formal significance test is added.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results and plotted findings are retained. Table 3 adds 20 no-PE results, including bidirected-GIN Gain RMSE of 0.386±0.008. Table 19 adds SAT-labelled results, but all 12 mean-and-uncertainty pairs exactly match Table 1's corresponding DAG SPE entries despite the different stated backbone; whether these represent independent results is unclear.

T1.justification: The walk-profile definitions, Theorems 4.1–4.2, Appendix A proofs and normalized-walk-profile definition are retained. Removing stray braces in Equations 3–4 is a typographical correction without a change to the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about walk profiles, existing PE limitations, Multi-q expressiveness and stable complex-eigenvector processing.

C2.justification: New Appendix F interprets its comparison as showing that a strong SAT backbone cannot fully compensate for older PEs' distance-representation limitations. Existing computational-cost limitations and discussion of directly using walk profiles remain unchanged, with the latter moved from Appendix F to G.

D1.justification: The added distance comparison specifies SAT with a bidirectional GIN encoder and SPE processing, providing limited configuration information. Existing implementation tables, hardware and training-time disclosures, and the code link are unchanged. No dedicated hyperparameter table accompanies the new comparison.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Qitong Wang et al.'s Directed graph transformers as prior work using singular-vector positional encodings. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 updates the publication header, makes limited wording and equation-typography corrections, and inserts a short Appendix F, renumbering the former F–G as G–H. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains no-PE rows and revised highlighting, and Table 19 is added. Figures 1–2 are reduced in size, while Table 2, Figure 3 and Table 3 move within the main text. Existing figure content and plotted curves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 3's no-PE controls make the contribution of positional encodings easier to assess, while its revised annotations give context about winning margins relative to variability. These provide a limited improvement to the retained evaluation. The added SAT study carries uncertain additional evidential value because Table 19 exactly repeats Table 1's SPE results under a different stated architecture.
